findings.title: AI model file-write blocks are expanded into shell commands without quoting or heredoc hardening, allowing arbitrary command execution.
Terminal AI FILE blocks resolve paths without project-boundary checks, allowing writes outside the opened project via traversal or absolute paths.
Swarm automation defaults auto-approve agent confirmation prompts, including file overwrite requests, without blocking sensitive out-of-project paths.
Project file enumeration follows repository symlinks and loads out-of-project files into AI context sent to external providers.
resolveAiWritePath validates string prefixes but not symlink targets, so AI file writes can escape the opened project through symlinked paths.
Velix injects stored AI provider API keys into every PTY shell environment, enabling exfiltration by malicious project scripts.
Swarm post-task validation automatically executes repository npm/yarn build, test, and lint scripts without user confirmation.
Swarm launches Claude Code workers with --dangerously-skip-permissions, disabling all CLI tool permission gates by default.
Terminal AI suggested-command shortcuts execute model-controlled shell commands on a single digit keypress with no confirmation dialog.
get_git_diff passes attacker-controlled file paths to git diff without a -- separator, enabling option injection that writes diff output to arbitrary repo paths.
Velix Git panel operations execute repository git hooks without sandboxing, enabling arbitrary command execution from malicious project .git metadata.
Terminal npm Tab-autocomplete suggests attacker-controlled package.json scripts, enabling trojan command execution after Tab+Enter.
AI-powered terminal autocomplete embeds attacker-controlled package.json script names in the model prompt, enabling trojan shell command execution after Tab+Enter.
Terminal npm Tab-autocomplete interpolates unquoted package.json script names, enabling shell command injection via malicious script keys.
Custom worker CLI commands are stored and launched without shell quoting or metacharacter validation, enabling arbitrary command execution.
git_checkout_branch passes branch names to git checkout without a -- separator, so a malicious -f branch ref is parsed as the force flag and discards uncommitted work.
Velix get_git_diff runs git diff without disabling repository-configured external diff drivers, enabling arbitrary command execution when the Git panel loads file diffs.
Velix Git checkout executes repository-configured smudge/clean filter drivers without sandboxing, enabling arbitrary command execution when switching branches.
Velix git fetch and pull execute repository-configured credential helpers without sandboxing, enabling arbitrary command execution.
Velix git pull executes repository-configured merge drivers without sandboxing, enabling arbitrary command execution when pulls merge divergent branches.
Velix git push executes repository-configured credential helpers without sandboxing, enabling arbitrary command execution.
Swarm launches Gemini, Codex, and Copilot workers with permission-bypass flags that disable CLI tool approval gates.
Velix get_git_status runs git status without fsmonitor sandboxing, enabling arbitrary command execution from repository core.fsmonitor configuration.
Velix git fetch and pull execute repository-configured core.sshCommand without sandboxing, enabling arbitrary command execution when contacting SSH remotes.
Velix git fetch executes ext:: transport URLs when repository config enables protocol.ext.allow, enabling arbitrary command execution.
Velix git fetch and pull execute repository-configured core.askpass helpers without sandboxing, enabling arbitrary command execution when authentication is required.
Velix git push executes ext:: transport URLs when repository config enables protocol.ext.allow, enabling arbitrary command execution.
Velix git push executes repository-configured core.sshCommand without sandboxing, enabling arbitrary command execution when contacting SSH remotes.
Velix git pull executes ext:: transport URLs when repository config enables protocol.ext.allow, enabling arbitrary command execution.
Project file search follows repository symlinks and reads out-of-project files into Search panel results.
Swarm worker spawn feeds prompt files through double-quoted $(cat ...) command substitution, letting attacker-controlled assignment tasks break out and execute arbitrary shell commands.
Tool Panel project analysis follows repository symlinks during directory scans and uploads the resolved out-of-project file contents to external AI providers.
Velix ai_chat sends Gemini API keys in the request URL query string, exposing secrets to proxies and log sinks.
Velix persists all provider API keys as plaintext JSON in the application config settings file on disk.
Swarm SafetyLimiter path and command guardrails are never invoked during agent execution, leaving forbidden-path and forbidden-command controls inert.
Swarm Dry Run mode is stored in configuration but never checked before spawning agents or running validation, so runs still mutate the repository.
Swarm post-task validation automatically runs npx tsc in the repository without user confirmation, enabling arbitrary code execution via trojan TypeScript binaries.
Velix git push upstream setup passes the current branch name to git push without a -- separator, so attacker-controlled branch names like --force are parsed as git options.
Terminal yarn/pnpm Tab-autocomplete hardcodes dev script execution, enabling trojan package.json scripts after Tab+Enter.
AutomationPanel dispatch and broadcast build shell commands with breakable single-quote escaping, enabling arbitrary command execution from crafted automation goals or subtask prompts.
Terminal git Tab-autocomplete steers users into git commit/checkout commands that execute unsandboxed repository hooks configured via core.hooksPath or .git/hooks.

Terminal npm/yarn/pnpm Tab-autocomplete runs package managers without neutralizing repository .npmrc script-shell/node-options or .yarnrc.yml yarnPath hijacks, enabling arbitrary command execution even when package.json scripts are benign.
Terminal cargo Tab-autocomplete runs cargo build/run without neutralizing repository .cargo/config.toml rustc-wrapper or target runner hijacks, enabling arbitrary command execution.
Terminal git log/branch Tab-autocomplete executes git through a PTY without disabling repository core.pager, enabling arbitrary command execution.
Terminal git diff Tab-autocomplete executes git through a PTY without disabling repository-configured external diff drivers, enabling arbitrary command execution.
WorkspaceService scans follow repository symlinks via get_all_files and load symlinked out-of-project file contents into AI prompts sent to external providers.
Terminal git fetch Tab-autocomplete executes git fetch through a PTY without sandboxing repository-configured credential helpers, ext:: transports, core.sshCommand, or core.askpass.
Swarm automation auto-approves npm/yarn/pnpm install, build, and test worker confirmation prompts, enabling execution of malicious repository package scripts without user confirmation.

Terminal git pull, push, and merge Tab-autocomplete execute git through a PTY without sandboxing repository-configured credential helpers, merge drivers, hooks, ext:: transports, core.sshCommand, or core.askpass.
Terminal Tab-autocomplete maps partial input `re` to `git rebase` and executes it through a PTY without sandboxing repository rebase hooks.

Swarm post-task validation runs npm/yarn through execute_shell_command without neutralizing repository .npmrc script-shell/node-options or .yarnrc.yml yarnPath hijacks, enabling arbitrary command execution even when package.json scripts are benign.
Terminal npm install Tab-autocomplete completes partial install commands and runs npm install, executing attacker-controlled package lifecycle scripts after Tab+Enter.
Terminal git clone Tab-autocomplete steers users into git clone executed through a PTY without sandboxing credential helpers, smudge/clean filters, or ext:: transport handlers.

Velix get_git_remote_info treats any origin URL containing a github.com substring as a GitHub repository, hiding the real remote and displaying false GitHub branding that misleads users into push/pull against an attacker host.
